zara: Heads-up — after the kernel-profile swap last night (attn-tiling-v2 + quant-profile=fast128) we saw a sustained drop in prompt-warm hit-rate on prod. Rough numbers below and a short flamegraph link.

mike: can you drop the top-line numbers + which model fleets are affected? 70B only or everything?

zara: quick snapshot from 00:00-02:00 UTC:
```
prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.62 -> 0.44  # aggregated across endpoints
70B_v1_hit_rate: 0.65 -> 0.43
13B_v2_hit_rate: 0.59 -> 0.48
p50_decode_latency_tokens: 12ms -> 18ms
kernel: attn-tiling-v2
quant_profile: fast128
deploy_tag: kernel/attn-tiling-v2/2026-03-17
```
link: https://perf.internal/redwood/flame/1768661200 (flamegraph shows heavy time in key-serialization)

ravi: I profiled the KV key fingerprints on canary and see a distribution shift. The new kernel serializes past_key tensors with a trailing stride reorder; our fingerprint routine hashed raw bytes, so identical logical contexts now get different fingerprints ~12% of the time. Quick stats:
```
before: collisions ~0.03% | mean_bucket_size 1.01
after:  collisions ~0.35% | mean_bucket_size 1.12
key_fingerprint_bits: 64 -> 56 (effective entropy loss)
```

mike: that explains both hit-rate drop and increased p50 (more cold starts). Also noticed batching heuristic "adaptive-slab" groups by runtime-seq_len now (kernel sets seq_len metadata later in pipeline) — batches are merging prompts that previously were isolated, which changes prefix keys created by the warmup prefetcher.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back kernel/attn-tiling-v2 from nodepools: gke-infer-1a,gke-infer-1b,gke-infer-2a at 01:24 UTC :white_check_mark:

sam: I pushed a tiny runtime patch to normalize key serialization (kc-normalize) that canonicalizes tensor layout before fingerprinting. Rolling canary -> 5% now.
/deploy runtime canary --tag kc-normalize --percent 5

zara: after canary (30m) metrics improved but not fully back to baseline: aggregated hit_rate 0.62 -> 0.57. Looks like two contributors: (1) key serialization mismatch (partially fixed), (2) batching heuristic change that modifies which prefixes get primed. Next steps: revert kernel on remaining fleets until batching-order fix or make prefetcher compute keys earlier in the pipeline. Filing follow-up evals + perf runbook.

mike: filing ticket PERF-7123 with attachments (flame, profiles, sample keys). tagging eng-runtime, eng-runtime-batching, eng-ml for model-layout review. @ravi can you attach the raw fingerprint diffs to the ticket?

ravi: on it, uploading diffs now :point_down:
https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/1768661234/key-diffs.tar.gz

zara: thanks — keeping this thread open. Will update when we have full rollback or batching fix. :eyes:
